findings.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — Unescaped `url` is interpolated into `#{url}` inside a raw_html post; an attacker-chosen embed_url like `http:///?x'onmouseover='alert(1)` parses fine with URI (single quote is unreserved), the host check passes, the page fetch returns 200, and the payload becomes stored XSS in both the iframe and the main forum topic.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:16 — Any request with a spoofed Referer header (curl) and an unknown embed_url enqueues a RetrieveTopic job with no controller-side rate limit; the redis throttle is keyed per exact URL, so varying a query string yields unbounded job flooding, unbounded HTTP fetches of the embeddable host, and unbounded topic creation (one topic per `?x=N` variant).

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:34 — Feed item HTML is only CGI-unescaped, never sanitized, and stored as a raw_html post that bypasses Discourse's cook/sanitize pipeline, so any script/iframe/onerror in a third-party or compromised feed is executed on the forum origin for every reader.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:20 — check-then-create race: `where(embed_url).first` then `TopicEmbed.create!` under a unique index; concurrent RetrieveTopic jobs (staff bypass throttle, throttle expiry) or the hourly PollFeed racing a RetrieveTopic-triggered PollFeed raise RecordNotUnique, roll back the topic/post inside Topic.transaction, and leave already-enqueued post-process/notification jobs pointing at rolled-back rows.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:47 — Readability whitelist keeps `a[href]`/`img[src]` with no scheme check, and raw_html posts skip the sanitizer, so `javascript:` hrefs in a fetched page land as clickable XSS in the forum.

app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:9 — The loading page reloads every 30s forever with no cap; if retrieval can never succeed (wrong host in discourseEmbedUrl, 404, feed failure) every open browser tab enqueues a new RetrieveTopic job twice a minute indefinitely.

lib/topic_retriever.rb:42 — Each RetrieveTopic job synchronously runs the full PollFeed (fetch whole feed, re-import every item, PostRevisor per changed item), so a single spoofed embed request amplifies into N imports and it runs concurrently with the scheduled hourly job.

app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:8 — RetrieveTopic has no `retry: false`; `open(url)` raising on 404/timeout makes Sidekiq retry with default backoff, multiplying the fetch load from flooded/failing requests.

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:28 — open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` is Kernel#open; a value starting with `|` executes a shell command, turning admin site-setting write access into RCE on the Sidekiq host.

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:32 — No per-item rescue: a single item with nil `content` (NoMethodError on scrub) or a failing import aborts the whole loop, so one bad feed entry silently blocks all subsequent items from ever importing while the job appears to run.
app/models/topic_embed.rb:11 — ^https?://` uses line-anchored `^` (not `\A`), so a multi-line feed link/id such as `evil\nhttp://x` passes the check and is interpolated into href/HTML.

app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — Origin check is `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`, a substring/prefix test: an origin like `http://forum.example.co` matches `http://forum.example.com/`, and the unvalidated `e.data.height` lets any matching window resize the iframe arbitrarily.
lib/topic_retriever.rb:26 — setnx` followed by a separate `expire` is not atomic; if the worker dies in between the key never expires and that URL is permanently throttled for non-staff.
app/models/topic_embed.rb:63 — start_with?('/')` treats protocol-relative `//cdn.example/x` as site-relative and rewrites it to `http://host/cdn.example/x`, breaking those links/images.

lib/tasks/disqus.thor:114 — The `--category`/`-c` option was removed from `disqus import` with no deprecation, so existing invocations silently lose their category (Thor drops unknown switches) and imported threads land in uncategorized.

lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — Topic creation now goes through `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which does a live HTTP fetch of every thread link via ruby-readability and returns nil for any non-http(s) link, so threads with unreachable/non-http links are silently skipped along with all their comments and the thread `created_at` is no longer honored.

app/models/post.rb:133 — Post#cook` now returns `raw` verbatim for `raw_html` posts, bypassing the `after_post_cook` plugin filter and the sanitize pipeline, changing the contract that `cooked` is always sanitized/plugin-filtered output.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — TopicEmbed.import` mutates the caller's `contents` string in place via `<<`, a hidden side effect on a public class method argument (and the appended footer feeds into `content_sha1`).

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:34 — i.content` is nil for RSS 2.0 items (simple-rss exposes `description`/`content_encoded`, not `content`), so the setting advertised as "RSS/ATOM" raises NoMethodError on plain RSS feeds; `String#scrub` also requires Ruby >= 2.1.
app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:7 — Embedders must set `discourseUrl` with a trailing slash or the iframe src becomes `hostembed/best`; this undocumented contract is easy to get wrong.

app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — Origin check is a substring match (`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)`), so it accepts messages from any origin whose string appears in `discourseUrl` (e.g. `http://a.com` when discourseUrl is `http://a.com.evil.net/`), rather than an exact origin comparison.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:28 — X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` is not a valid header value; framing only works because browsers ignore invalid values, which is fragile and should instead omit the header (or use CSP frame-ancestors).

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — i.content` is nil for RSS 2.0 items (SimpleRSS exposes content:encoded as `content_encoded`, `content` only for Atom), so `.scrub` raises NoMethodError and aborts the whole hourly poll (retry: false)

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 — No per-item rescue: one bad feed item (nil content, HTTP/DB error in TopicEmbed.import) aborts all remaining items in the feed and the synchronous TopicRetriever path
app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — String#scrub` only exists on Ruby >= 2.1; on the Ruby 2.0 this codebase targets it raises NoMethodError
app/models/topic_embed.rb:63 — Protocol-relative URLs (`//cdn.example.com/x.png`) start with '/' and get rewritten to `http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png`, breaking links/images

app/models/topic_embed.rb:33 — embed.post` can be nil (post trashed under Trashable default scope or destroyed); `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` then raises NoMethodError on every subsequent poll for that URL
app/models/topic_embed.rb:47 — open(url).read` has no error handling; an HTTPError/timeout in import_remote propagates and aborts the caller (RetrieveTopic job, whole Disqus import loop)

app/models/topic_embed.rb:51 — doc.title` may be nil and `skip_validations: true` bypasses title checks, so topic creation hits the NOT NULL constraint on topics.title / empty slug instead of a clean failure
lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — setnx` then `expire` are not atomic; if the process dies between them the `retrieved:<url>` key never expires and non-staff retrieval of that URL is throttled forever

app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 — Concurrent retrievals (e.g. two staff-triggered RetrieveTopic jobs, or PollFeed racing a job) both pass the `exists?` check; the second `TopicEmbed.create!` violates the unique index and raises after creating a post, rolling back but surfacing an unhandled RecordNotUnique
lib/tasks/disqus.thor:147 — Switching to import_remote drops the Disqus thread `created_at` (topics now dated at import time) and silently returns nil for non-http links, skipping all their comments

app/models/topic_embed.rb:23 — When `PostCreator#create` fails (e.g. TopicCreator error) `import` silently returns nil with no logging; combined with the loading page reloading every 30s and enqueuing a job per request, this becomes an unbounded, invisible retry loop with no failure state.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:41 — Concurrent imports of the same URL (hourly PollFeed vs. inline PollFeed from RetrieveTopic) race to `TopicEmbed.create!`; the loser raises RecordNotUnique out of the transaction after `PostCreator` already published via MessageBus and enqueued process_post jobs for a post that is then rolled back.

app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:9 — The loading page reloads unconditionally every 30s forever with no cap or backoff, so every viewer of a URL whose import keeps failing generates perpetual requests and job enqueues.

app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:17 — Staff viewers bypass the throttle entirely (`no_throttle: staff?`), so a staff user sitting on a failing embed triggers a full feed download plus remote page fetch every 30s.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — The only gate on `embed/best` is a Referer host match, which any non-browser client forges trivially, so unauthenticated attackers can enqueue RetrieveTopic for arbitrary URLs on the embeddable host (every distinct query string is a new topic created as `embed_by_username` with `skip_validations`, and the redis throttle in lib/topic_retriever.rb:26 is per-URL so it does not limit this).

app/models/post.rb:134 — cook_method` persists on the post, so any later edit of an embedded post (by the non-admin `embed_by_username` account or any editor via PostRevisor, lib/post_revisor.rb:83) writes arbitrary unsanitized HTML straight into `cooked`, letting a low-privilege user XSS every viewer.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:45 — open(url).read` (open-uri) on a user-chosen path of the embeddable host follows HTTP redirects with no timeout/size cap, so any open redirect on that host turns the Sidekiq worker into an SSRF proxy to internal HTTP services, and the fetched body is stored as trusted raw HTML.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:46 — Readability whitelist keeps `href`/`src` attributes without URL-scheme filtering, so `javascript:` links in the remote page survive into raw_html cooked output and execute on click in both the embed iframe and the forum.

lib/post_revisor.rb:85 — Behavioral change (save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])) has no spec in post_revisor_spec verifying that skip_validations bypasses validations or that the default path still validates.

app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:9 — Jobs::RetrieveTopic has no spec: missing embed_url raising InvalidParameters, user lookup, and staff -> no_throttle mapping are all untested.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:43 — import_remote (ruby-readability parsing, title override via opts) has no coverage and is now the only code path used by the disqus importer.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the diff appends `contents << "...#{url}..."` and then creates a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. The diff also changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == ...[:raw_html]`, and the embed view renders posts with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. The only URL validation in `import` is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, so an attacker-controlled URL containing a single quote (e.g. in the query string) can break out of the single-quoted `href` attribute and inject arbitrary attributes/HTML, producing stored XSS in the topic and iframe.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:16 — Any request with a spoofed Referer header (curl) and an unknown embed_url enqueues a RetrieveTopic job with no controller-side rate limit; the redis throttle is keyed per exact URL, so varying a query string yields unbounded job flooding, unbounded HTTP fetches of the embeddable host, and unbounded topic creation (one topic per `?x=N` variant).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `EmbedController#best` which enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil, with no controller-side throttling (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). The only gate is `ensure_embeddable`, which trusts `request.referer`/Origin host matching `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (spoofable by a client). In the job path, `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` throttles on a Redis key that is the full `@embed_url` string (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so varying query strings (`?x=N`) yields unique keys and bypasses the 60s throttle (lib/topic_retriever.rb). `TopicEmbed.import`/`import_remote` then creates a new topic/embed per unique URL (unique index is on `embed_url`), so an attacker can flood jobs and cause unbounded HTTP fetches and topic creation for that host.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:34 — Feed item HTML is only CGI-unescaped, never sanitized, and stored as a raw_html post that bypasses Discourse's cook/sanitize pipeline, so any script/iframe/onerror in a third-party or compromised feed is executed on the forum origin for every reader.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a raw HTML ingestion path for feed imports that bypasses Discourse’s normal cooking/sanitization. In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, feed item content is only `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and then passed to `TopicEmbed.import`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts via `PostCreator.new(... raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents), skip_validations: true, cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])`. In `Post#cook`, `raw_html` returns `raw` directly, skipping the rendering/sanitization pipeline. As a result, arbitrary HTML (including `<script>`, event handlers like `onerror`, iframes, etc.) from a compromised/third-party feed would be stored and rendered, enabling XSS on the forum origin.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:20 — check-then-create race: `where(embed_url).first` then `TopicEmbed.create!` under a unique index; concurrent RetrieveTopic jobs (staff bypass throttle, throttle expiry) or the hourly PollFeed racing a RetrieveTopic-triggered PollFeed raise RecordNotUnique, roll back the topic/post inside Topic.transaction, and leave already-enqueued post-process/notification jobs pointing at rolled-back rows.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code does a non-atomic check-then-act: `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, later `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)` inside a transaction. The migration `create_topic_embeds` adds `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`, so concurrent callers can both observe `embed.blank?` and then the second will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` at `create!`, rolling back the enclosing `Topic.transaction` (including the newly-created post/topic). The diff also introduces multiple concurrent entry points that can call `TopicEmbed.import`/`import_remote` (e.g., `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` and the scheduled `Jobs::PollFeed`, plus `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` only checks `exists?` before fetching, which is also racey), and there is no rescue/upsert/locking to make this safe.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:47 — Readability whitelist keeps `a[href]`/`img[src]` with no scheme check, and raw_html posts skip the sanitizer, so `javascript:` hrefs in a fetched page land as clickable XSS in the forum.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` where `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly (app/models/post.rb), bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` fetches arbitrary remote HTML via `open(url).read` and uses ruby-readability with `attributes: %w[href src]` (app/models/topic_embed.rb), then imports `doc.content` into a post with `cook_method: :raw_html` and later renders it with `raw post.cooked` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb). There is no scheme validation/sanitization shown for `href`/`src`, so a remote page containing `href="javascript:..."` would be stored and rendered as clickable HTML, creating an XSS vector.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:9 — The loading page reloads every 30s forever with no cap; if retrieval can never succeed (wrong host in discourseEmbedUrl, 404, feed failure) every open browser tab enqueues a new RetrieveTopic job twice a minute indefinitely.

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when no TopicEmbed exists it always enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). The loading view unconditionally `document.location.reload()` after 30000ms with no stop condition (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb), so if an embed can never be created (e.g., invalid/mismatched embed_url host causes TopicRetriever.invalid_host? to short-circuit, or remote fetch fails), the page will keep re-requesting /embed/best and enqueueing a new RetrieveTopic job every 30s per open tab. TopicRetriever's Redis throttle only prevents the actual retrieve work, not the repeated job enqueues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:42 — Each RetrieveTopic job synchronously runs the full PollFeed (fetch whole feed, re-import every item, PostRevisor per changed item), so a single spoofed embed request amplifies into N imports and it runs concurrently with the scheduled hourly job.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb `perform_retrieve` unconditionally runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` whenever `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, before attempting `fetch_http`. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) fetches the entire feed (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`) and iterates all `rss.items`, calling `TopicEmbed.import` for each item (potentially revising posts). Because `RetrieveTopic` jobs call `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, any embed retrieval can synchronously trigger a full-feed import, duplicating work with the hourly scheduled PollFeed and creating an amplification/DoS risk when multiple RetrieveTopic jobs run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:8 — RetrieveTopic has no `retry: false`; `open(url)` raising on 404/timeout makes Sidekiq retry with default backoff, multiplying the fetch load from flooded/failing requests.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` without `sidekiq_options retry: false` (app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb). That job can indirectly call `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which does `open(url).read` (app/models/topic_embed.rb) and can raise on network errors/404/timeouts. With Sidekiq’s default retry behavior, failures would be retried with backoff, increasing fetch attempts/load during failures or floods. This is an operational/robustness concern grounded in the diff, not a deterministic functional bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:28 — open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` is Kernel#open; a value starting with `|` executes a shell command, turning admin site-setting write access into RCE on the Sidekiq host.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Jobs::PollFeed` which does `require 'open-uri'` and then calls `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` (poll_feed.rb). Using `open` on a string is dangerous because `Kernel#open` treats values starting with `|` as a shell command (pipe), so a malicious `feed_polling_url` site setting could trigger command execution in the Sidekiq process. This is a concrete security issue introduced by the new feed polling feature and its new admin-controlled setting (`config/site_settings.yml`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:32 — No per-item rescue: a single item with nil `content` (NoMethodError on scrub) or a failing import aborts the whole loop, so one bad feed entry silently blocks all subsequent items from ever importing while the job appears to run.
app/models/topic_embed.rb:11 — ^https?://` uses line-anchored `^` (not `\A`), so a multi-line feed link/id such as `evil\nhttp://x` passes the check and is interpolated into href/HTML.

adjudication.rationale: In new `TopicEmbed.import`, the URL validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` (line ~11). In Ruby, `^` can match after a newline, so a string like `"evil\nhttp://x"` would satisfy the regex even though it’s not a clean URL. That untrusted `url` is then interpolated into HTML (`<a href='#{url}'>`) when appending `imported_from`, so a multiline value can pass the guard and be embedded into rendered HTML.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — Origin check is `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`, a substring/prefix test: an origin like `http://forum.example.co` matches `http://forum.example.com/`, and the unvalidated `e.data.height` lets any matching window resize the iframe arbitrarily.

adjudication.rationale: In new `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the message handler uses `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`, which is a substring/prefix match rather than an exact origin comparison. If `discourseUrl` is e.g. `http://forum.example.com/`, an attacker origin `http://forum.example.co` would pass because it is a prefix substring. After passing that check, `e.data.height` is used directly to set `iframe.height` with no numeric/range validation, allowing arbitrary resizing by any window that can satisfy the weak origin check. This is a verifiable security/correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:26 — setnx` followed by a separate `expire` is not atomic; if the worker dies in between the key never expires and that URL is permanently throttled for non-staff.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle key is created with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and only afterwards a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` is issued. If the process/worker dies after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key will persist without a TTL, causing `setnx` to return false forever and the URL to remain permanently throttled for non-staff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:63 — start_with?('/')` treats protocol-relative `//cdn.example/x` as site-relative and rewrites it to `http://host/cdn.example/x`, breaking those links/images.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, both link and image rewriting use `href.start_with?('/')` / `src.start_with?('/')` and then rewrite to `"#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}"` (same for `src`). Protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example/x` do start with `/`, so they will be incorrectly rewritten to something like `http://host/cdn.example/x`, breaking those URLs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:114 — The `--category`/`-c` option was removed from `disqus import` with no deprecation, so existing invocations silently lose their category (Thor drops unknown switches) and imported threads land in uncategorized.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` and deletes the associated `category_id` lookup and `category: category_id` argument previously passed to `PostCreator`. The new code calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which (per the diff) does not accept or apply any category. This is a concrete backward-incompatible behavior change/regression in the CLI task, but the claim that Thor will "silently" drop unknown switches is not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — Topic creation now goes through `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which does a live HTTP fetch of every thread link via ruby-readability and returns nil for any non-http(s) link, so threads with unreachable/non-http links are silently skipped along with all their comments and the thread `created_at` is no longer honored.

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, topic creation was changed from `PostCreator.new(... created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]) ...)` to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`.import` do not pass or set `created_at`, so the imported thread timestamp is no longer honored. Also, `TopicEmbed.import` explicitly returns `nil` unless `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, and the Thor task only processes comments inside `if post.present?`, so non-http(s) thread links will result in the thread (and its comments) being skipped without further handling in this code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:133 — Post#cook` now returns `raw` verbatim for `raw_html` posts, bypassing the `after_post_cook` plugin filter and the sanitize pipeline, changing the contract that `cooked` is always sanitized/plugin-filtered output.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Post.cook_methods` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which bypasses `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` and the normal cooking/rendering path (`post_analyzer.cook`). The new embedding/import flow sets `cook_method: :raw_html` for imported content (e.g., `TopicEmbed.import` via `PostCreator`), and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Since `PollFeed` ingests `i.content` from an external feed without any sanitization/whitelisting before storing, this introduces a concrete risk of unsanitized HTML being served, matching the finding’s contract-change concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — TopicEmbed.import` mutates the caller's `contents` string in place via `<<`, a hidden side effect on a public class method argument (and the appended footer feeds into `content_sha1`).

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/topic_embed.rb, TopicEmbed.import does mutate its `contents` argument in place via `contents << "\n<hr>..."` before computing `content_sha1`. This is a real, diff-grounded hidden side effect on a public method parameter and could surprise callers if they reuse the same string instance, but the diff doesn’t show this causing incorrect behavior or a failure (the mutation appears intentional to include the footer in the stored content/hash).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:34 — i.content` is nil for RSS 2.0 items (simple-rss exposes `description`/`content_encoded`, not `content`), so the setting advertised as "RSS/ATOM" raises NoMethodError on plain RSS feeds; `String#scrub` also requires Ruby >= 2.1.
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that calling `i.content.scrub` can fail because `i.content` is often nil for many RSS feeds (especially RSS 2.0), leading to a NoMethodError/nil exception, and that a fallback (e.g., to `description`) is needed. Candidate adds extra detail about simple-rss fields and Ruby version, but the core issue matches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:7 — Embedders must set `discourseUrl` with a trailing slash or the iframe src becomes `hostembed/best`; this undocumented contract is easy to get wrong.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the iframe URL is built via simple concatenation: `iframe.src = discourseUrl + "embed/best?embed_url=" + ...`. If `discourseUrl` is configured without a trailing `/`, this produces an invalid path like `https://forum.example.comembed/best...` (no separator). The diff contains no normalization (e.g., ensuring `discourseUrl` ends with `/`) or documentation/guard in code, so the embed script can break depending on how the host sets `discourseUrl`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — Origin check is a substring match (`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)`), so it accepts messages from any origin whose string appears in `discourseUrl` (e.g. `http://a.com` when discourseUrl is `http://a.com.evil.net/`), rather than an exact origin comparison.
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that the origin validation relies on a substring/indexOf check, which can be bypassed by crafting a malicious domain that contains the expected domain as a substring (or vice versa), instead of doing an exact origin match.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:28 — X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` is not a valid header value; framing only works because browsers ignore invalid values, which is fragile and should instead omit the header (or use CSP frame-ancestors).

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, the diff explicitly sets `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"`. `ALLOWALL` is not a standard/valid `X-Frame-Options` value (common valid values are `DENY` and `SAMEORIGIN`, with `ALLOW-FROM` being obsolete). Using a nonstandard value risks inconsistent browser behavior and can break or weaken framing controls; allowing embeds should instead be done by omitting the header or using CSP `frame-ancestors`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — i.content` is nil for RSS 2.0 items (SimpleRSS exposes content:encoded as `content_encoded`, `content` only for Atom), so `.scrub` raises NoMethodError and aborts the whole hourly poll (retry: false)

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the code does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If `i.content` is `nil` for any feed item, calling `.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the poll loop. The diff adds no nil-guard or fallback (e.g., `i.content_encoded`, `i.description`, etc.), and the job is configured `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so a single bad/missing-content item would stop polling until the next run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 — No per-item rescue: one bad feed item (nil content, HTTP/DB error in TopicEmbed.import) aborts all remaining items in the feed and the synchronous TopicRetriever path

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, rss.items.each do |i| processes items without any per-item rescue. The code calls i.content.scrub and TopicEmbed.import(...) (which can raise, e.g., nil i.content => NoMethodError, network/DB/PostCreator exceptions, or create! failures). Any exception will abort the loop and, because TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) synchronously when feed_polling_enabled, it can also abort the TopicRetriever retrieval path before falling through to fetch_http.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — String#scrub` only exists on Ruby >= 2.1; on the Ruby 2.0 this codebase targets it raises NoMethodError

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, which directly calls `String#scrub` with no fallback/guard. If this app runs on a Ruby version that lacks `scrub` (e.g., < 2.1), this line will raise `NoMethodError` during feed polling, breaking the job.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:63 — Protocol-relative URLs (`//cdn.example.com/x.png`) start with '/' and get rewritten to `http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png`, breaking links/images

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, both link and image rewriting use `if href.present? && href.start_with?('/')` (and same for `src`). Protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x.png` also start with '/', so they will be rewritten to `"#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}"`, producing `http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png` instead of preserving `//cdn.example.com/x.png` or converting to `http(s)://cdn...`. This breaks such links/images and is a correctness defect in the new logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:33 — embed.post` can be nil (post trashed under Trashable default scope or destroyed); `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` then raises NoMethodError on every subsequent poll for that URL

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `post = embed.post` and then unconditionally calls `PostRevisor.new(post)` when `content_sha1` differs. If the referenced post record is missing (e.g., deleted) then `embed.post` will be `nil`, and `PostRevisor` will later dereference `@post` (e.g., `@post.acting_user = ...` / other methods), raising `NoMethodError` and preventing further imports/updates for that `embed_url`. The diff shows no validation of `post_id` presence at the model level and no guard/recovery when `embed.post` is nil.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:47 — open(url).read` has no error handling; an HTTPError/timeout in import_remote propagates and aborts the caller (RetrieveTopic job, whole Disqus import loop)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, `open(url).read` is called with no `rescue` around it (and `open-uri`/network IO can raise `OpenURI::HTTPError`, `Timeout::Error`, socket errors, etc.). This method is invoked from `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` (used by `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`) and from the Disqus Thor task (`TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)`), so an exception will propagate and fail the Sidekiq job / abort the import loop as the finding states.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:51 — doc.title` may be nil and `skip_validations: true` bypasses title checks, so topic creation hits the NOT NULL constraint on topics.title / empty slug instead of a clean failure

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, the title passed to `TopicEmbed.import` is `opts[:title] || doc.title` (no fallback). If `doc.title` is nil/blank, `TopicEmbed.import` then calls `PostCreator.new(..., title: title, ..., skip_validations: true, ...)`, so presence validations won’t prevent creating a topic/post with a missing title. That can lead to an exception (e.g., downstream nil/blank title handling or DB NOT NULL constraints) rather than a controlled failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — setnx` then `expire` are not atomic; if the process dies between them the `retrieved:<url>` key never expires and non-staff retrieval of that URL is throttled forever

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle key is set with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and only then given a TTL via `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These are two separate Redis commands; if the process crashes or the connection drops after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the `retrieved:<url>` key will persist without expiration, permanently throttling non-staff retrieval for that URL. This defect is directly visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 — Concurrent retrievals (e.g. two staff-triggered RetrieveTopic jobs, or PollFeed racing a job) both pass the `exists?` check; the second `TopicEmbed.create!` violates the unique index and raises after creating a post, rolling back but surfacing an unhandled RecordNotUnique

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, creation is guarded only by `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and later `TopicEmbed.create!` under a unique index on `embed_url`. With concurrent imports (e.g., PollFeed + RetrieveTopic, or two jobs), both can observe `embed.blank?` and both will attempt `create!`; the second will raise an unrescued unique-constraint exception (RecordNotUnique). Although wrapped in `Topic.transaction` (so the post/topic would roll back), the job/request would still error due to the unhandled exception. The earlier `exists?` checks in TopicRetriever don’t eliminate this race.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:147 — Switching to import_remote drops the Disqus thread `created_at` (topics now dated at import time) and silently returns nil for non-http links, skipping all their comments

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor the importer now does `post = TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` instead of `PostCreator.new(..., created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), ...)`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` -> `TopicEmbed.import` does not pass any `created_at`, so the created topic/post will default to the import time. Also `TopicEmbed.import` begins with `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, so non-http(s) `t[:link]` causes a nil return; the Disqus importer only proceeds with comments inside `if post.present?`, so those threads' comments will be skipped with no explicit error handling in the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 — <%- end if %>` leaves a dangling `if` modifier whose condition becomes the next generated ERB output statement; it only works because that expression happens to be truthy

app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — contents <<` mutates the caller's string (raises on frozen input) and is done before the sha1, so the stored hash depends on the current I18n footer text/locale rather than the article content

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import` the line `contents << "\n<hr>..."` mutates the passed-in `contents` string in place. That can raise `FrozenError` if the caller supplies a frozen string, and it also means callers observe their input changed unexpectedly. Additionally, `content_sha1 = Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(contents)` is computed after appending an I18n-translated footer (`I18n.t('embed.imported_from', ...)`), so the “did the article change?” hash is sensitive to the current translation/locale text, not just the fetched article body; changing the translation/locale could spuriously trigger updates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:76 — embed_url lookup is an exact string match; trailing slash, query string or fragment variants of the same page create separate topics and separate scrapes

adjudication.rationale: Verified in diff: TopicEmbed.import does `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and topic_id_for_embed does `where(embed_url: embed_url)` with no URL normalization (no stripping of trailing slash, query params, or fragments). Therefore different string representations of the same page will be treated as distinct embeds and can create separate topics/scrapes. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:11 — topic_id_for_embed returns ids of deleted topics, so TopicView raises NotFound and the embed is permanently broken with no re-retrieval path

With Sidekiq’s default retry behavior, a permanently failing `embed_url` would be retried many times over time, and because `retrieved_recently?` only throttles for 60 seconds via Redis, retries occurring later will re-fetch again.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:13 — If the topic behind a TopicEmbed row is deleted, `topic_id_for_embed` still returns its id and `TopicView.new` raises NotFound, leaving that embed_url permanently broken with no path to re-import (no cleanup of topic_embeds on topic destroy).

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, it uses `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` and if non-nil immediately calls `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` with no check that the referenced topic still exists. `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` is just `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: embed_url).pluck(:topic_id).first`, so an orphaned `topic_embeds` row (e.g., topic deleted) will still return an id. Additionally, `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` bails out early if `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?`, so the presence of the orphaned row prevents re-import/recreation. The diff shows no `dependent: :destroy` or cleanup on topic deletion, making the embed_url effectively stuck/broken.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:26 — setnx` followed by a separate `expire` is not atomic; if the process dies between them the throttle key never expires and non-staff retrieval of that URL is blocked until redis is flushed.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle uses `setnx` and then a separate `expire` (`if $redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`). These two Redis operations are not atomic; if the process crashes or the connection drops after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key can be left without a TTL, permanently causing `retrieved_recently?` to return true for non-staff and blocking retrieval for that URL until the key is manually cleared.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:23 — When `PostCreator#create` fails (e.g. TopicCreator error) `import` silently returns nil with no logging; combined with the loading page reloading every 30s and enqueuing a job per request, this becomes an unbounded, invisible retry loop with no failure state.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, when `embed.blank?` it calls `creator = PostCreator.new(...); post = creator.create` and only creates the `TopicEmbed` row if `post.present?`; if `create` returns nil, the method just returns nil with no logging or failure marker (no rescue/log/flag) (`app/models/topic_embed.rb`, around the transaction). In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil it enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading` (`app/controllers/embed_controller.rb`), whose JS forces a reload every 30s (`app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`). This combination can produce an endless “loading” state and repeated job enqueues per page reload/request when the import keeps failing, with no visible error state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:41 — Concurrent imports of the same URL (hourly PollFeed vs. inline PollFeed from RetrieveTopic) race to `TopicEmbed.create!`; the loser raises RecordNotUnique out of the transaction after `PostCreator` already published via MessageBus and enqueued process_post jobs for a post that is then rolled back.

adjudication.rationale: `TopicEmbed.import` does a non-atomic check-then-create (`embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` followed by `TopicEmbed.create!`) while the migration adds a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`. With concurrent importers (scheduled `Jobs::PollFeed` and `TopicRetriever` calling `PollFeed`/`import_remote`), two workers can both see `embed.blank?` and then one will hit `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` on `create!`. The specific claim about MessageBus/process_post side effects happening before the transaction rolls back is not verifiable from this diff, but the race/exception on unique constraint is.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:9 — The loading page reloads unconditionally every 30s forever with no cap or backoff, so every viewer of a URL whose import keeps failing generates perpetual requests and job enqueues.

adjudication.rationale: In app/views/embed/loading.html.erb the script unconditionally calls `document.location.reload()` every 30000ms with no stop condition. When `EmbedController#best` can’t find a `topic_id` it renders this loading page and *also* enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` on every request. So if retrieval/import keeps failing (or is slow), each viewer will generate repeated requests and repeated job enqueues indefinitely (at least every 30s), even though the job itself may throttle retrieval via `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:17 — Staff viewers bypass the throttle entirely (`no_throttle: staff?`), so a staff user sitting on a failing embed triggers a full feed download plus remote page fetch every 30s.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does implement a staff throttle bypass: `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` passes `no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)` to `TopicRetriever` (app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb), and `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` returns `false` immediately when `@opts[:no_throttle]` is set (lib/topic_retriever.rb). When an embed isn’t found, `EmbedController#best` enqueues `:retrieve_topic` and renders `loading`, whose JS reloads the page every 30s (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb). On each reload, a staff user would enqueue another job that can run `Jobs::PollFeed` (full feed download via `open(...)`) and then `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (remote page fetch via `open(url)`) without the 60s Redis throttle. This is a real, diff-grounded performance/resource-usage concern, though not a correctness defect per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — The only gate on `embed/best` is a Referer host match, which any non-browser client forges trivially, so unauthenticated attackers can enqueue RetrieveTopic for arbitrary URLs on the embeddable host (every distinct query string is a new topic created as `embed_by_username` with `skip_validations`, and the redis throttle in lib/topic_retriever.rb:26 is per-URL so it does not limit this).

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil it enqueues `:retrieve_topic` even for anonymous users (`user_id: current_user.try(:id)` can be nil). The only access control shown is `ensure_embeddable`, which checks `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and sets `X-Frame-Options = ALLOWALL`; the Referer header is client-controlled and forgeable. `TopicRetriever` then allows any `embed_url` whose host matches `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, and its throttle key is `retrieved:#{@embed_url}` (full URL), so varying query strings bypasses throttling. `TopicEmbed.import_remote/import` can create new topics/posts as `embed_by_username` with `skip_validations: true`, so this endpoint can be abused to mass-create content for arbitrary distinct URLs on the embeddable host.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — url` is interpolated unescaped into `#{url}` and stored as raw_html cooked; the url is attacker-controlled via `embed_url` (only host/scheme are checked, and `'` is a legal URI char) so `http://host/x'onmouseover='alert(1)` yields stored attribute/HTML injection rendered by `raw post.cooked` in the embed and by the main forum client.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, `url` is only gated by `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` and is then interpolated directly into HTML: `"#{url}"` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). Because posts created here use `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and Post#cook returns `raw` unchanged for `:raw_html`, this HTML is stored and later rendered unsanitized (e.g., app/views/embed/best.html.erb uses `raw post.cooked`). Since `'` is valid in a URL, a value like `http://eviltrout.com/x'onmouseover='alert(1)` can break out of the single-quoted href attribute and inject arbitrary attributes/HTML, leading to stored XSS. Host checks in TopicRetriever don't prevent this because the malicious URL can still have the allowed host.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:34 — RSS item content is `CGI.unescapeHTML`'d and imported with `cook_method: raw_html`, so it is stored verbatim as `cooked` with no sanitization (scripts, event handlers, javascript: URLs) and rendered as trusted HTML forum-wide; any compromised or third-party-authored feed content becomes stored XSS.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a `cook_method` enum with `:raw_html` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`, and `Jobs::PollFeed` passes `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` straight into `TopicEmbed.import` with no sanitization/whitelisting. As a result, arbitrary HTML from an RSS/Atom feed can be stored as `cooked` verbatim and later rendered (e.g., embed view uses `<%= raw post.cooked %>`), enabling stored XSS if feed content includes scripts/handlers/javascript: URLs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:134 — cook_method` persists on the post, so any later edit of an embedded post (by the non-admin `embed_by_username` account or any editor via PostRevisor, lib/post_revisor.rb:83) writes arbitrary unsanitized HTML straight into `cooked`, letting a low-privilege user XSS every viewer.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a persistent `posts.cook_method` and changes `Post#cook` to return `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` and `skip_validations: true` using HTML from RSS (`i.content`) or `ruby-readability` (`doc.content`) without sanitization, and the embed view renders `raw post.cooked` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb). Since `cook_method` persists and `PostRevisor` does not reset it on edit, any later revision of such a post will continue to bypass the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline, allowing arbitrary HTML to be stored into `cooked` and rendered, enabling XSS by whoever can edit that post (including the non-admin `embed_by_username` author).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:45 — open(url).read` (open-uri) on a user-chosen path of the embeddable host follows HTTP redirects with no timeout/size cap, so any open redirect on that host turns the Sidekiq worker into an SSRF proxy to internal HTTP services, and the fetched body is stored as trusted raw HTML.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, the diff adds `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` which uses open-uri on the passed `url` with no explicit timeout/size limits. The only host check in the new retrieval flow (`TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`) validates the *initial* `@embed_url` host against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, but does not constrain or re-validate the final destination after HTTP redirects, which open-uri will follow. That makes the worker potentially usable as an SSRF primitive via an open redirect on the allowed host. Additionally, imported content is persisted and rendered as `raw_html` (`PostCreator ... cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `Post#cook` returns `raw`), matching the finding’s “trusted raw HTML” concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:46 — Readability whitelist keeps `href`/`src` attributes without URL-scheme filtering, so `javascript:` links in the remote page survive into raw_html cooked output and execute on click in both the embed iframe and the forum.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which fetches remote HTML (`open(url).read`), extracts `doc.content` with Readability allowing `a`/`img` tags and `href`/`src` attributes, then imports it as a post with `cook_method: :raw_html` (bypassing the cooking/sanitization pipeline in `Post#cook`) and renders it via `raw post.cooked` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`. The diff itself contains no URL-scheme validation for `href`/`src` (it only rewrites relative URLs starting with '/'), so any `javascript:` (or similar) URLs present in the extracted HTML would be persisted and served to clients.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — postMessage origin check is `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`, a substring test rather than an equality/origin comparison (e.g. `http://forum.example.co` or any prefix origin passes), so the resize handler accepts messages from non-Discourse origins.

adjudication.rationale: In new `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the message handler uses `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`, which is a substring/prefix check rather than an exact origin comparison. If `discourseUrl` is `http://forum.example.com/`, an origin like `http://forum.example.co` will yield `indexOf(...) === 0` and incorrectly pass the check, allowing non-Discourse origins to trigger the resize behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` is `Kernel#open`, so a value beginning with `|` executes a shell command on the worker; admin-only setting but it makes an admin site setting a code-execution vector (also applies to `open(url)` in lib/tasks/disqus.thor via import_remote).

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the diff adds `require 'open-uri'` and then calls `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`; using `Kernel#open` on a string is dangerous because a value starting with `|` will execute a shell command and return an IO. Since `feed_polling_url` is an admin-controlled SiteSetting, this makes that setting a code-execution vector on the Sidekiq worker. The same pattern exists in TopicEmbed.import_remote (`open(url).read`), which is invoked from lib/tasks/disqus.thor via `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:19 — "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" only stub one setting while feed_polling_enabled stays at its default false, so both pass even if those guard conditions are deleted from PollFeed#execute.

In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, the tests "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" only stub one setting each (feed_polling_url or embed_by_username) but do not stub feed_polling_enabled? to true. Since the new site setting feed_polling_enabled defaults to false (config/site_settings.yml), PollFeed#execute will not call poll_feed regardless, so those tests would still pass even if the corresponding guard checks were removed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:23 — poll_feed itself (SimpleRSS parsing, link-vs-id fallback, CGI.unescapeHTML/scrub, TopicEmbed.import call) has zero coverage; the spec only checks dispatch to a mocked poll_feed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial logic in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb#poll_feed` (fetching `embed_by_username` user, `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`, iterating items with `link` vs `id` fallback, `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and calling `TopicEmbed.import`). The only added spec (`spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb`) asserts gating/dispatch behavior by mocking `poll_feed`, and does not exercise any of the parsing/import logic inside `poll_feed`, so that code path has no direct test coverage in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:133 — New raw_html cook_method bypasses the entire sanitize/cook pipeline yet has no Post-level spec; nothing verifies that feed content with <script> or event handlers is not stored verbatim into cooked (PollFeed passes unsanitized feed HTML straight into import).

The embed view renders `raw post.cooked` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb), so any `<script>`/event-handler HTML in the feed can be stored and served as-is, creating a verifiable XSS vector. adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:8 — "is 404 without an embed_url" passes for the wrong reason: embeddable_host is blank by default so ensure_embeddable raises InvalidAccess before params.require ever runs; assertion should_not be_success cannot distinguish 403 from 404.

(which is the default unless stubbed). In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb, the example "is 404 without an embed_url" does not stub embeddable_host, so the request will fail due to the before_filter rather than params.require(:embed_url). adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:42 — Test relies on Jobs.enqueue executing Jobs::RetrieveTopic inline (queue_jobs test:false) to satisfy TopicRetriever.expects(:new); it is implicitly coupled to that setting and never asserts that the job was enqueued with user_id/embed_url or that no_throttle is derived from staff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:50 — TopicView.expects(:new) returns nil and controller specs do not render views, so best.html.erb (including the suspicious `<%- end if %>` on line 6 and post.user/post.url calls) is never exercised by any test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_revisor.rb:85 — Behavioral change (save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])) has no spec in post_revisor_spec verifying that skip_validations bypasses validations or that the default path still validates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:41 — "Supports updating the post" only checks cooked =~ /new contents/; it does not assert the same post/topic is reused, that content_sha1 is updated, or that re-importing identical content skips the revision (the sha1 short-circuit branch is untested).

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (app/models/topic_embed.rb) which fetches and parses remote HTML via `open(url).read` and `Readability::Document`, with optional title override via `opts[:title]`. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:55 — absolutize_urls edge cases untested: non-80/443 port prefix, protocol-relative "//host/x" URLs (start_with?('/') matches and produces "http://host/host/x"), and https urls.
